statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-75805 ("NULL Pointer Dereference in CMP Client Revocation Response Handling", Low): a CMP client that requests revocation by PKCS#10 CSR (OSSL_CMP_exec_RR_ses() with OSSL_CMP_CTX_set1_p10CSR(), or openssl cmp -cmd rr -csr) sends no issuer or serial number and dereferences a NULL pointer when a malicious or compromised CMP server, or a man-in-the-middle holding the protection secret, names a certificate in its response. OpenSSL 3.5 is affected and fixed in OpenSSL 3.5.9; the FIPS modules are not affected because the CMP implementation is outside the FIPS module boundary. https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260929.txt, fix on the openssl-3.5 branch https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/9eb2a8a9b86136cdb39d6d7d50644dd66941cdc3, first released in OpenSSL 3.5.9. Debian fixed it for trixie in openssl 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 (DSA-6531-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-75805). The DHI Debian 13 openssl packages are rebuilds of Debian's trixie openssl, published in the DHI Debian repository and the DHI enterprise repository (the FIPS builds, and the openssl-provider-fips package of every build, only in the enterprise repository); the Debian changelog shipped in each libssl3t64 package shows which Debian release a build is based on. That changelog was read from every published build on amd64 and arm64: 25 versions, 17 standard and 8 FIPS builds, based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1. No build based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 or 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, FIPS builds included, names CVE-2026-75805. The first published rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, the fixed boundary here, and every later build, FIPS builds included, carry Debian's 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 entry naming it. The libcrypto in every one of these builds, on both architectures, exports OSSL_CMP_exec_RR_ses() and OSSL_CMP_CTX_set1_p10CSR(). Of the FIPS providers, the openssl-provider-fips package, read from every build on both architectures, ships the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider in the FIPS builds and the FIPS provider from the build's own OpenSSL release (3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9) in the other builds; the advisory places the affected code outside the FIPS module boundary, and the FIPS builds' libcrypto and libssl are Debian's 3.5 libraries checked above.
